scope: Framing-only benchmark on an owner-provided 1-vCPU Linux host; discard connection, no TLS or network throughput measurement
methodology: Both test executables include identical benchmark/test sources. Baseline replaces only production ws_stream.go with origin/main through a compile overlay. Run before/after/after/before in independent processes on the same Linux host.
limitations: Measures server-side header-only binary-message framing, not TLS, socket throughput or tunnel latency.
Masked client-side messages still use Gorilla's normal writer; no client-side allocation reduction is claimed.
The discard connection never blocks. Actual WS/WSS client/server wire and error behavior are verified by the regressions.
The remaining allocation is retained by the pooled Gorilla write path; this is not an allocation-free claim.
No race-enabled native run was performed in the Windows cross-compilation environment.
native_tests: Five repetitions of ^Test(WSMux|WebSocketStream|ConcurrentMux|MuxSession) passed. Temporary test files were removed.
